subject: Sprint-close capacity decision matrix and MAP: Veridium reserve plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Anita Rao <anita@veridiumhealth.com>, CloudOps <cloudops@veridiumhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sprint-close capacity decision matrix and MAP: Veridium reserve plan

Anita / CloudOps team —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As promised, I attached a starter MAP worksheet (veridium_map_v1.xlsx) that pairs evaluation gates with the capacity reservation decisions we recommend to avoid an availability pinch during your Q4 ramp. High-level asks below; details in the attachment.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Pilot phase (6–8 week POC): reserve a 4-GPU pool (H100-equivalent) to validate throughput & latency targets against your highest concurrency flows. Lead time: 10–12 weeks for hosted Dedicated pools.
- Scale tranche 1 (production canary): reserve +4 GPUs (total 8) to support steady-state peak for the first tranche. Lead time: additional 8–12 weeks; we recommend staggering delivery.
- Scale tranche 2 (full production): plan for 16 GPUs total (or equivalent mixed tranche with hybrid Dedicated + Private nodes) for your expected 2x growth runway — procurement lead time for Private (on-prem/VPC) options typically 18–24 weeks.

Tradeoffs / gating:
- If we need to shorten lead time: accept quantized model variants (8-bit) + more aggressive batching and a 10–15% quality delta on edge cases.
- If latency is non-negotiable: prioritize lower-latency model variants and increase pool size to reduce queuing.

Next steps I propose (action items for MAP):
- You confirm acceptance of the phased tranche approach (POC -> canary -> scale) and preferred tranche dates.
- Veridium Procurement: we need a standard SOW + PO window that aligns with the tranche ship dates in the attachment.
- CloudOps: confirm network/VPC readiness and any on-prem delta that would affect lead times.

I’ll schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock milestone dates once you confirm.

Attachments: veridium_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + decision matrix), gpu-supply-timeline.pdf (supply lead-time notes)

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

PS — Ben: looping you so we can get ops feasibility early on for tranche staging.

Marissa —

Thanks, this looks like a solid start. A couple quick clarifications so I can brief our CFO and Procurement:

1) The 4 / 8 / 16 GPU progression — are those H100-equivalent units (we'll need explicit SKU equivalents for budget).
2) Can the first tranche be delivered in two smaller deliveries (2 + 2) to shorten the visible lead time?
3) For Private on-prem, do you have an end-to-end ship / install estimate vs just hardware lead time? Procurement prefers a single integrated ETA.

I've looped Procurement so they can start preparing a PO template. If you can send a short decision matrix with SKU mapping and two alternate timelines (aggressive vs standard) that would help.

Anita
VP, Engineering — Veridium Health
anita@veridiumhealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 13:40:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Sprint-close capacity decision matrix and MAP: Veridium reserve plan

Anita —

Thanks for the quick review. I've attached a short decision matrix in the workbook and pasted the SKU + timeline options below so Procurement can pick one. I also included an "aggressive" path that shortens visible lead time by using split deliveries + quantized model fallback for the POC.

SKU mapping (recommended equivalents):
- H100-equivalent: 80GB H100 or 2x 40GB H100 (model dependent on memory footprint).
- A100-equivalent: 40GB A100 (used for lower-cost batch workloads).

Timeline options:
- Standard: POC reserve (4 H100-eq) ship in 10–12 weeks; tranche 1 (+4) in additional 8–12 weeks; tranche 2 (scale to 16) another 10–14 weeks (total ~28–38 wks to full).
- Aggressive (recommended if you need earlier capacity): split first tranche into 2 + 2 (two 2-GPU deliveries) to reduce initial visibility to 6–8 weeks for the first mini-delivery. Accept quantized 8-bit variants for the POC to reduce memory pressure.

Suggested MAP milestones (dates are placeholders until you confirm):
- 2027-06-01: POC kickoff (contract SOW executed).
- 2027-07-15: POC performance gate (latency <120ms p95 on target flow).
- 2027-08-01: Canary tranche deploy (first 4 GPUs in production canary).
- 2027-10-01: Tranche 2 capacity increase to 16 GPUs if usage tracks projected ramp.

Operational notes (for Ben / Priyom / Irene):
- We'll pair each tranche with a canary traffic profile and golden prompt set for quality regression checks.
- Autoscaling policy: we recommend minimum pool size pinned to reserved GPUs, with burst capacity enabled for ephemeral needs.

Attachments in this message: veridium_map_v1.xlsx (decision matrix), gpu-supply-timeline.pdf (supply notes). Let me know if you want me to produce a single integrated ETA (ship + install + acceptance) for Private / on-prem — we can do that with our solutions team.

—
Marissa

Subject: RE: Sprint-close capacity decision matrix and MAP: Veridium reserve plan

Marissa / team —

Operational feasibility notes from infra:
- Staged deliveries (2 + 2) are possible for Hosted Dedicated but we need explicit PO windows to secure factory allocation. Shortening beyond that requires accepting preemption risk or moving to mixed-architecture (A100 + H100).
- For Private on-prem we will provide an integrated ETA that includes hardware ship + rack & install + connectivity validation. Typical integrated ETA: 20–26 weeks from signed SOW depending on data center carrier lead times.
- Autoscaling + quantized fallback: we can instrument a canary that automatically routes matched traffic to the quantized variant on overload, with a quality-monitoring hook that will surface regressions to your CS/ML teams.

I'll work with Ben to draft the runbook for tranche cutovers and DR/fallback steps.

—
Priyom
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwoodinference.com
